title: Relative module Hom over a Noetherian algebraic-space base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to B$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces, locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], and quasi-separated, meaning that its relative diagonal is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests. Assume $B$ is Noetherian: it is quasi-compact, its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact, and every etale scheme chart is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Quasi-compactness of a space means admitting a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme. Let $F,G$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], both of finite type, meaning etale locally generated by finitely many sections. Suppose $G$ is flat over $B$: after etale scheme charts of $B$ and of their pullback of $X$, every ordinary module stalk is flat over the corresponding local ring of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Suppose $G$ has support proper over $B$, meaning that there are a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z\to B$ proper and a finite type quasi-coherent module $N$ on $Z$ with $i_*N\simeq G$ [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For each scheme $T\to B$, put $X_T=X\times_BT$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and let $F_T,G_T$ be ordinary tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. The functor $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X_T}}(F_T,G_T)$ is represented by an algebraic space $H\to B$, naturally in all schemes $T\to B$, and $H\to B$ is affine and of finite presentation. Affine means that every affine scheme base change has affine scheme source. Finite presentation means locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts, quasi-compact, and quasi-separated. No properness or flatness of $f$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08JY (lemma-noetherian-hom), in Situation 08JT (situation-hom); proper closed-carrier formulation agrees with spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0CZI (lemma-module-support-proper-over-base).

proof.text: Choose the proper closed carrier $Z$ for $G$. Its point space is quasi-compact: $B$ has a finite quasi-compact atlas and the proper map $Z\to B$ is quasi-compact. Affine etale charts of $X$ have open quasi-compact images by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover, lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. Finitely many of these images cover $|Z|$; let $U\subseteq X$ be their union. It is a quasi-compact open subspace containing $Z$. For every $T\to B$, the complement of $U_T$ has $G_T=0$: [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-support-pullback] identifies its support with the inverse image of the support of $G$, contained in $|Z|$. Restriction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{X_T}(F_T,G_T)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{U_T}(F_T|_{U_T},G_T|_{U_T})$. The inverse glues the given map on $U_T$ with the zero map on the open complement of $\operatorname{Supp}(G_T)$; they agree on the overlap, where the target is zero. This construction commutes with tensor pullback. Thus replace $X$ by $U$. The carrier remains the same proper space $Z$.

source.place: Tag 08JY, first sentence; Tags 04NN and 07TZ, explicit finite-open-cover and sheaf-gluing argument

proof.text: The chartwise locally-finite-type hypothesis and [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] imply that $X$ is locally Noetherian. Since $f$ and $B$ are quasi-separated, [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] implies that $X$ is quasi-separated, also after the open restriction of step 1. Hence the restricted $X$ is Noetherian. The same node shows $X\times_B V$ is quasi-compact for every affine scheme $V\to B$ (all three factors are quasi-compact and quasi-separated), so $f$ is quasi-compact as well as quasi-separated. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus], the modules of sections of $F,G$ on Noetherian affine etale charts are finitely generated. They are coherent: a submodule of any finite free module over a Noetherian ring is finitely generated. They are finitely presented as well, since the kernel of a finite free presentation is finitely generated. These observations check the coherence and finite-presentation hypotheses needed below without assuming properness or flatness of $f$.

source.place: Tag 08JY, first paragraph; Tag 04ZK via scheme charts, Tag 073B, Tag 07UB

proof.text: Regard $F$ as a complex concentrated in degree zero. It has coherent cohomology and is bounded above, so [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-pseudocoherent-criterion] makes it pseudo-coherent. Apply [lem-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-perfect-approximation] to $E=F[0]$ and $a=-1$. It supplies a perfect $P$ and $u:P\to F[0]$ such that $\mathcal H^0(u)$ is an isomorphism and $\mathcal H^i(P)=0$ for all $i>0$.

source.place: Tag 08JY, perfect approximation of (X,F,-1); Tags 08IK and 08HP

proof.text: For a scheme test $g:T\to B$, write $h:X_T\to X$ and $P_T=Lh^*P$. Then $P_T$ is perfect, nonpositive, and the canonical map $P_T\to Lh^*F[0]\to F_T[0]$ induces $\mathcal H^0(P_T)\simeq F_T$. Here is the local calculation, including the potentially nonflat case: on an affine etale chart represent $P$ by a bounded finite-projective complex. Since its positive cohomology vanishes, split off its exact positive tail successively from the highest degree, giving a bounded finite-projective representative in degrees at most zero. Tensor pullback computes $P_T$ on these representatives. It has no positive terms and its zeroth cohomology is $\operatorname{coker}(h^*d^{-1})=h^*\operatorname{coker}(d^{-1})=h^*F$ by right exactness of tensor. The constructions on overlaps agree because the map used is the canonical map induced by $u$ and the ordinary-pullback comparison. No assertion $Lh^*G=G_T$ is used.

source.place: Tag 08JY, second displayed Hom comparison and its explanation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-nonpositive-derived-hom] on the ringed small etale site of each $X_T$ to $E=P_T$ and $M=G_T$. The preceding isomorphism $\mathcal H^0(P_T)\simeq F_T$ identifies the canonical precomposition map with a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X_T}}(F_T,G_T)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_{X_T})}(P_T,G_T[0])$. It is natural in $T$: for any further base change, both routes pull back a module map and precompose with the pulled-back map $u$, and tensor-pullback composition identifies these maps. The same lemma says that $R\mathcal Hom(P_T,G_T)$ has no negative cohomology sheaves.

source.place: Tag 08JY, two Hom comparisons and final nonnegative internal-Hom observation

proof.text: Set $K=Rf_*R\mathcal Hom(P,G)$. By [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality], $P^\vee$ is perfect and $R\mathcal Hom(P,G)\simeq P^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}G$. The finite-type proper-carrier hypothesis on $G$ is equivalent to proper scheme-theoretic support by [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support]. Therefore [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-tensor-perfect] applies to $E=P^\vee$ and the complex $G[0]$: the base is Noetherian, $f$ is locally finite type and quasi-separated, and $G$ is coherent, relatively flat, and has proper support. It follows that $K$ is perfect.

source.place: Tag 08JY, K is perfect; Tag 0DKK proved by Tags 08JJ and 0DKJ; support convention Tag 0CZI

proof.text: For every scheme test $g:T\to B$, apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-coefficient-rhom-base-change] to the quasi-compact quasi-separated $f$, perfect $P$, and relatively flat quasi-coherent $G$. This gives the canonical natural isomorphism $Lg^*K\simeq Rf_{T,*}R\mathcal Hom(P_T,G_T)$ in $D(\mathcal O_T)$. In particular the right-hand coefficient is the ordinary tensor pullback $G_T$, even when $g$ is nonflat. This is precisely why the hypothesis is flatness of $G$ over $B$, rather than flatness of $f$.

source.place: Tag 08JY, displayed base-change isomorphism; Tag 08JQ, case (1)

proof.text: By step 5, $R\mathcal Hom(P_T,G_T)$ is in degrees at least zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] to the left exact module direct image $f_{T,*}$ to conclude $\mathcal H^i(Lg^*K)=0$ for $i<0$, using step 7. Left exactness holds because the specified module direct image is a right adjoint [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. The module categories are Grothendieck by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and the lower bound puts this application in $D^+$ even though the ambient categories are unbounded.

The global Hom formula [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] identifies the derived Hom set in step 5 with $H^0(X_T,R\mathcal Hom(P_T,G_T))$. The canonical ringed-topos models [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] permit applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $f_T$ followed by global sections (the map to the terminal topos with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$). Consequently this is $H^0(T,Rf_{T,*}R\mathcal Hom(P_T,G_T))\simeq H^0(T,Lg^*K)$ by step 7. All these maps are natural: the Hom formula, derived composition, and the canonical base-change comparison identify pullback of a morphism with pullback of its derived global-section class. Thus the original Hom functor is naturally isomorphic to $T\mapsto H^0(T,Lg^*K)$.

source.place: Tag 08JY, Leray identifications; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 08JA and 0D6E

proof.text: The complex $K$ is perfect by step 6 and every scheme pullback has no negative cohomology by step 8. Apply [lem-sfb-space-connective-perfect-sections-affine]. It represents $T\mapsto H^0(T,Lg^*K)$ by an algebraic space affine and of finite presentation over $B$. Compose its representing bijections with the natural identifications in steps 1, 5 and 9. The resulting bijections represent the original Hom functor on all schemes over $B$, proving every asserted clause.
